Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the run chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and the Indian players can be seen in a huddle. Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmanullah Gurbaz are set to open the innings for Afghanistan as Rohit Sharma has not taken the field. It looks like Virat Kohli might be captaining for now. Mukesh Kumar will take the new ball for India and he is raring to go and Shubman Gill is on the field for Rohit.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

India has posted a mammoth total of 212 on the board and surely has an upper hand here. They will aim to bundle up the opposition as soon as possible. Whereas, Afghanistan has a tough task up its sleeves and has a very steep slope to climb. The run chase is just a few moments away. Stay tuned.

Afghanistan on the other hand, had Indian eyes lit up straightaway as they dismantled the Indian top order as Fareed Ahmad got rid of Yashasvi Jaiswal, Virat Kohli and Sanju Samson with his excellent 3-fer. He ended up with brilliant figures by conceding only 20 in his spell when the others were being hammered away. Azmatullah Omarzai chipped in with a scalp of Shivam Dube and they had India on the back foot in the first half. But, the tables turned sooner as the debutant Mohammad Saleem was taken to the cleaners and the Afghanistan bowlers sort of lost their momentum halfway into the innings and offered freebies to Rohit and Rinku. The last five overs proved to be an absolute nightmare for them and it was a poor execution after a brilliant initiation. Afghanistan couldn't take any wickets after the fifth over of the innings and just leaked runs all over the ground.

Wow, just wow! That was power-hitting of the highest quality. We have witnessed a scintillating knock by the Indian skipper Rohit Sharma after losing four wickets in the initial stages on the mere score of 22. India saw the early departures including Yashasvi Jaiswal, followed by Virat Kohli and Sanju Samson, both of whom were dismissed without scoring a run. The next to fall was Shivam Dube, who had effortlessly smashed sixes in the previous game. Rohit Sharma, coming into this game on the back of a couple of ducks, started off a bit tentatively but sooner got into his groove along with Rinku Singh, who, equally contributed crucial runs in the partnership. India rebuilt pretty well as the two started taking the bowlers apart with some brutal hits out of the park and complemented each other brilliantly. India had an exceptional recovery as Rohit garnered a brilliant century and scored his highest T20I score. Rinku Singh, as calm as a cucumber, accumulated a phenomenal FIFTY. He scored a blistering 69 and 36 coming off the last over. Rinku Singh and Rohit Sharma together struck 14 sixes. India garnered 103 runs in the last five overs and also breached the 200 mark which, looked impossible to achieve at the start.

SIX! Make that five maximums and 36 runs off the over! What an epic finish from India and Afghanistan have been left red-faced here. Karim Janat changes the angle by coming in from around the stumps and digs it in a bit short and angling into the hitting arc. Rinku Singh stays put and just swivels on it a bit before pulling it over deep mid-wicket for a maximum. India finish with a mammoth total of 212/4 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: It's time for a quick breather and what an hour or so of play we have had here at Chinnaswamy! India would definitely need that pause as they were rocked early losing four wickets upfront. Of what looked like a high-scoring pitch, India started off with losing Jaiswal early and he was followed by Virat Kohli and Sanju Samson, both getting out on golden ducks. The next to depart was Shivam Dube, who smoked sixes like a cakewalk in the previous game. Rohit Sharma and Rinku Singh are out in the middle and they have faired well against the tide. They would aim to build a good partnership from here. Afghanistan came up with a plan to bowl on hard lengths and stuck to it and executed them pretty well. Fareed Ahmed has picked a brilliant 3-fer and has had the Indian eyes lit up. An interesting next half of the first innings is on the cards. Stay tuned.

Commentary.Commentary: Turn straightaway! Nicely floated up on a nagging length and outside off, the ball just grips and turns away as Rohit Sharma pulls out of the block.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Qais Ahmad to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Time for spin as Qais Ahmad comes into the attack now!

Great commitment in the deep! Nice and full on the legs, Rinku Singh clips it away with good timing and in front of deep mid-wicket as well but the fielder speeds across the turf and dives in to save a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Azmatullah Omarzai to Rinku Singh, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length in the channel outside off, Rohit Sharma taps it in front of point and races across for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Azmatullah Omarzai to Rohit Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Good take behind the stumps from Rahmanullah Gurbaz! Good length, spilled well down the leg side for a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Azmatullah Omarzai to Rohit Sharma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller in length and on the stumps again, Rohit Sharma looks to hit through the line of the ball but gets a big inside edge onto the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Azmatullah Omarzai to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Risky, very risky from Rohit Sharma! Drags the length back and bowls it over middle, angling it back in, Rohit shimmies down the pitch and has a big swipe across the line but misses it completely.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Azmatullah Omarzai to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches it right up on off and middle, Rohit Sharma shows the full face of the bat and defends it on the front foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Azmatullah Omarzai to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Cut and cut really hard! Just a fraction short and wide, Rohit Sharma latches onto the width and slaps it away past point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Azmatullah Omarzai to Rohit Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length and angling into the right-hander, Rinku Singh defends it back to the bowler. An end of a successful over from Fareed Ahmad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Fareed Ahmad to Rinku Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Holds on the nagging length and a bit short, Rinku Singh looks to tuck it away towards square leg but he is hit on the pads. A bit of yes or no from the batters and they decide to abort the run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Fareed Ahmad to Rinku Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and around off, Rinku Singh pushes it towards cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Fareed Ahmad to Rinku Singh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Rinku Singh is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Sanju Samson departs on a golden duck and India are four down on just 22! Short ball into the pitch, Sanju Samson goes for a big one right away and loses his shape completely on that one, and gets a leading edge which flies straight in front Mohammad Nabi who is stationed at covers and he takes a good grab. India are reeling at the moment as Fareed Ahmad picks up his third wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Nabi b Fareed Ahmad
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Fareed Ahmad to Sanju Samson, OUT! c Mohammad Nabi b Fareed Ahmad.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length again around off, Rohit Sharma steers it to third man for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Fareed Ahmad to Rohit Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and on off, Rohit Sharma looks to pull but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Fareed Ahmad to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sanju Samson walks out to bat with India in a spot of bother.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Shivam Dube departs now! India are rocked early! Back of a length and Azmatullah Omarzai gets this one to move further away outside off, Shivam Dube looks to defend it but gets an outside edge which flies to the left of Rahmanullah Gurbaz who takes a fine catch behind the wickets. Dube perishes cheaply and Afghanistan are right on the top of proceedings now.
Commentary.Howout: c Rahmanullah Gurbaz b Azmatullah Omarzai
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Azmatullah Omarzai to Shivam Dube, OUT! c Rahmanullah Gurbaz b Azmatullah Omarzai.

Commentary.Commentary: In the air...and safe! No timing at all on that one. Length delivery into the pitch and right into the slot of Rohit, he looks to go over the mid-wicket boundary and ends up hitting on the bottom half of the blade and the ball lobs up in the air but lands in the safe zone somewhere over mid on. They cross for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Azmatullah Omarzai to Rohit Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Another one on a hard length with a hint of an outswing after pitching, Rohit Sharma stands tall and hits it straight to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Azmatullah Omarzai to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls on a tight length on the pads and does not give him any room, Shivam Dube looks to flick it but misses and ends up getting hit on the pads. They cross for a leg-bye single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Azmatullah Omarzai to Shivam Dube, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: On a back of a length angling into the batter again, Shivam Dube looks to work it towards leg side but gets a thud on his pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Azmatullah Omarzai to Shivam Dube, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Over the wicket and on a hard length which swings into the batter, Shivam Dube defends it to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Azmatullah Omarzai to Shivam Dube, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Onto the pads on a back of a length, Shivam Dube gets off the mark nudging it away to backward square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Fareed Ahmad to Shivam Dube, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a back of a length outside off, Shivam Dube defends it to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Fareed Ahmad to Shivam Dube, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shivam Dube walks in to face the hat-trick delivery.

OUT! CAUGHT! Would you believe it? Virat departs on the first ball and there's a pin drop silence at Chinnaswamy! Bowls it on a hard length that sits up a bit, Virat Kohli is hurried into the shot and looks to pull it away. He ends up getting it off the higher part of the bat as the ball lobs straight up in the air and Ibrahim Zadran takes a crucial catch at mid off moving to his right. Virat Kohli is dejected and so are the fans at Chinnaswamy as they see their icon departing on a golden duck. India struggling at the moment.
Commentary.Howout: c Ibrahim Zadran b Fareed Ahmad
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Fareed Ahmad to Virat Kohli, OUT! c Ibrahim Zadran b Fareed Ahmad.

Commentary.Commentary: Virat Kohli walks in at number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT! That's a brilliant catch from Mohammad Nabi in the deep and India lose their first wicket. Bowls on a nagging length around middle and leg corridor, Yashasvi Jaiswal gets in position to smash it away over the leg side but does not get enough wood on it and ends up slicing it a bit. The ball stays in the air for a fair bit of time. Mohammad Nabi settles under it and takes a good grab around the mid-wicket region. Yashasvi Jaiswal departs early.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Nabi b Fareed Ahmad
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Fareed Ahmad to Yashasvi Jaiswal, OUT! c Mohammad Nabi b Fareed Ahmad.

Commentary.Commentary: Pace off a bit on that one and on a back of a length at the stump line, Rohit Sharma tucks it away nicely to mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Fareed Ahmad to Rohit Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! And it's from Rohit's willow! This is pitched around middle and off on a back of a length and angling away, Rohit Sharma stands tall and gets enough wood on it and carves it to the deep backward point region for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Fareed Ahmad to Rohit Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Short and nipping away from off, Yashasvi Jaiswal stays rooted in the crease and punches it towards covers off the back foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Azmatullah Omarzai to Yashasvi Jaiswal, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches this one on a nagging length again around middle-leg, Yashasvi Jaiswal gets on top of the ball and hits it straight to the point fielder. Still couldn't find the gap there.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Azmatullah Omarzai to Yashasvi Jaiswal, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slides away after pitching on the off stump channel on a good length, Yashasvi Jaiswal slashes it towards point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Azmatullah Omarzai to Yashasvi Jaiswal, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A bit of an outswing on offer on a good length outside off, Rohit Sharma finally gets off the mark with a dab towards the third man region with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Azmatullah Omarzai to Rohit Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Another dot. Azmatullah Omarzai bowls on a nagging length which moves into the right-hander from off, Rohit Sharma comfortably flicks it towards short mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Azmatullah Omarzai to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts off with a hint of an inward movement on a good length in front of the middle stump, Yashasvi Jaiswal tucks it away towards square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Azmatullah Omarzai to Yashasvi Jaiswal, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Azmatullah Omarzai to bowl from the other end. Also, while changing ends, Rohit Sharma asks the umpire whether he gave the first boundary off the thigh pad as there was bat involved and the skipper even jokes about how he has got two ducks in the last two outings.
Ends with a back of a length ball outside off, Rohit Sharma looks to lap it but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Fareed Ahmad to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR LEG BYES! Still not off the mark there. Bowls on a nagging length angling down leg, Rohit Sharma misses on the glance and it wears on his thigh pads to the fine leg fence for another leg bye boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Fareed Ahmad to Rohit Sharma, 4 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Play and a miss! Back of a length again and angling away after pitching, Rohit Sharma looks to defend on the front foot and misses it through to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Fareed Ahmad to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length around off, Rohit Sharma steers it down to the point region.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Fareed Ahmad to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR LEG BYES! On a good length angling into the pads, Rohit Sharma looks to flick it away to the leg side but gets thud on the pads and the ball ricochets and runs away to the fence for four leg-byes. The replays show that there was an inside edge and Sharma is a bit unlucky to still not have gotten off the mark in the series.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Fareed Ahmad to Rohit Sharma, 4 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Finds the gap straightaway! Starts off with a short delivery outside off, Yashasvi Jaiswal rides on the bounce and pierces the gap between cover and point, the fielder in the deep slides and does well to save one run for the team.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Fareed Ahmad to Yashasvi Jaiswal, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin! The two umpires are out in the middle and so are the two Indian openers, skipper Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal. Fareed Ahmad has the new ball in hand and will get proceedings underway here. Let's play...

Ibrahim Zadran, the captain of Afghanistan says that they would have bowled first and will look to execute their plans. Adds that so far there have been a lot of positives from this series and they will try to have a good one. Adds that they have made as many as four changes with Naveen-ul-Haq, Fazalhaq Farooqi, Mujeeb Ur Rahman and Noor Ahmad not playing.

The Indian skipper, Rohit Sharma says that they will bat first as they have bowled in the first two games and now they want to try different things. It has nothing to do with the pitch and they want to try out different combinations and test the bench strength. It has been a good series and it's another good opportunity for them to end the series on a positive note. Ends by informing that Axar Patel, Arshdeep Singh and Jitesh Sharma are out and Sanju Samson, Kuldeep Yadav and Avesh Khan are in.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran (C), Azmatullah Omarzai, Mohammad Nabi, Najibullah Zadran, Karim Janat, Gulbadin Naib, Sharafuddin Ashraf (In for Mujeeb Ur Rahman), Qais Ahmad (In for Noor Ahmad), Mohammad Saleem (On T20 debut) (In for Naveen-ul-Haq), Fareed Ahmad (In for Fazalhaq Farooqi).

India (Playing XI) - Rohit Sharma (C), Yashasvi Jaiswal, Virat Kohli, Shivam Dube, Sanju Samson (WK) (In for Jitesh Sharma), Rinku Singh, Washington Sundar, Ravi Bishnoi, Kuldeep Yadav (In for Axar Patel), Avesh Khan (In for Arshdeep Singh), Mukesh Kumar.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favor of India and Rohit Sharma has opted to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Deep Dasgupta is pitchside. He starts by saying that the ground is fairly above sea level and it is 60 meters and 66 meters on either side of the wicket with the straight boundary being 70 meters. Nick Knight joins him and says that at first glance, it looks like there are a lot of cracks but when you take a second look at it, the pitch is hard and there is some grass, and will be slightly two-paced. Reckons there are runs to be scored and India might want to bat first. DDS ends by saying that pace-off might be the way to go on this surface.

As for the tourists, things haven’t worked out in their favor this whole series as they have struggled to contain the Indian batters and have been pretty expensive with the ball in hand. They are definitely missing the services of their superstar spin maestro Rashid Khan. His void was felt in this series as he has the potential to turn the course of the match single-handedly. Their batters will need to build a strong foundation up top and play attacking cricket to pressure the hosts. In the form of Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmanullah Gurbaz, they do have a fearless opening pair but the top two need to play responsibly and step up and end this series on a positive note. Right then, the anticipation is building higher and higher and one can expect a galore of sixes and fours at the Chinnaswamy. Stay tuned as the Toss and the team sheets are just around the corner.

India have been rock solid thus far in the series and even when the opposition has looked dangerous, they have been able to come out on top with ease. Shivam Dube has been consistent in both games and has unleashed his potential with an aggressive approach and hitting with absolute precision. Arshdeep Singh and Axar Patel will aim to keep things tidy just as they have done so far. Indian skipper Rohit Sharma would like to have some runs by his name in this game as this is the last T20I for India before they enter the T20 World Cup, 2024 later this year in June. With Virat Kohli playing his habitual colossal strokes and Rinku Singh being consistent, the Indian batting order looks nothing less than lethal. With the series in the bag, we might just see a few changes to the Playing XI as well.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the 3rd and the final T20I between India and Afghanistan which is taking place at the Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru. India has already clinched the three-match series in a comprehensive way and leads by 2-0. Sixes and fours rained havoc at the Holkar Stadium in Indore as the two Indian southpaws, extremely talented Yashasvi Jaiswal, and the strong bloke Shivam Dube stepped up and helped India chase down a decent total of 172, with their 68 and 63 runs respectively. The visitors have threatened at times but haven't been able to take control of the two matches gone by and will be hoping to avoid a whitewash.
... MATCH DAY ...

The Chinnaswamy is all in readiness to witness an exciting clash between India and Afghanistan for the 3rd and the final T20I. India has already clinched the series 2-0 and has outplayed the tourists prodigiously. But this time, it's the youngsters who have stepped up and performed. The two southpaws, Yashasvi Jaiswal, and Shivam Dube batted with lightning speed at Indore and struck some mesmerizing strokes, taking the Afghan spinners to the cleaners and smoking the ball out of the park. Also, the two happen to be the leading run-scorers in the series by far. The crowd roared at its pinnacle as they got to witness Virat Kohli after a long wait in the shortest format. Though his stay at the crease was not long enough, he did play some eye-catching shots upfront and marked his statement. India chased down the target of 173 quite comfortably with around four overs to spare and didn't give Afghanistan any breathing space. Indian bowlers too, stepped up and picked crucial timely wickets and will aim to continue the same further. As for the visitors, Gulbadin Naib looked attacking but, he was stranded alone. Afghan spinners were pretty expensive as they were the victims of the Dube-Jaiswal onslaught. The void of Rashid Khan's experience is being felt by the Afghans. Now, coming into the third and final game, Afghanistan will look to finish the series on a consolation and keep their spirits higher. Given that Chinnaswamy is a relatively smaller ground, boundary scoring is anticipated to be abundant and a treat for the batters. We can also expect to see a few changes in both teams as they might want to test the bench strength too. India has the opportunity to whitewash Afghanistan and would aim to continue the brute force with the bat as this is their final T20I game before entering into the T20 World Cup in June later this year, so they will definitely bring their A-game. Will India sweep the series or will Afghanistan prevent the whitewash? Let the games begin...
